# Review backend ownership and boundaries

Apply Jason’s capability-first backend rules while keeping coordination explicit.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use when designing or reviewing a backend against this chosen model.

Example request:

> Review this service boundary using the existing backend rules; preserve local naming and propose the smallest migration.

Expected result: A boundary recommendation tied to the existing rules, code and concrete consequences.

## A concrete example

This illustrative example starts from the source facts below.

**Source facts and constraints:** Checkout and stock are separate owned capabilities. A workflow coordinates both through the existing application surface.

**Before**

> Put the checkout and stock workflows into a shared helper.

**After**

> Keep checkout and stock rules inside their capabilities. Coordinate the cross-capability workflow in the existing application surface.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.6.0 --skill backend-slice-architecture
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.

Read the [complete skill instructions](../../skills/backend-slice-architecture/SKILL.md) and [bundled purpose reference](../../skills/backend-slice-architecture/references/placement-and-contracts.md) for the full conditions and exceptions.

## Inspiration and local decisions

Jason’s original backend rules govern architecture. Microsoft and Google writing guidance improves their explanation; it does not add architectural requirements.
